picks.title: Slay the Spire 2 lead says the 'garbage' placeholder art is important and gen AI would ruin it
picks.excerpt: Mega Crit's lead argues that deliberately rough hand-made placeholder art is a vital part of the early-access design process, and that swapping it for polished generative-AI art would distort how players judge an unfinished game. A working designer's craft case for why gen AI doesn't fit their iteration workflow.
picks.rationale: A working studio's concrete craft argument for why rough placeholder art beats gen-AI polish during iteration — directly actionable for how designers run early-access playtesting and manage player perception.

picks.title: George Lucas Goes To The Dark Side, Says AI Is 'The Future'
picks.excerpt: Star Wars creator George Lucas compares refusing to use AI to riding a horse in the age of cars, calling the tech inevitable for creative work. A high-profile creator framing generative AI as an unavoidable shift — the kind of stance shaping how studios and creatives debate adopting it.
picks.rationale: A landmark creator's blunt 'AI is inevitable' framing sits opposite the same day's craft-refusal takes — high novelty and credibility, sharpening the adoption debate studios and creatives are having right now.

picks.title: 'Good games will get cloned and buried' – AI vibe coding is one of the biggest threats on storefronts like Steam, analyst warns
picks.excerpt: An industry analyst warns that AI 'vibe coding' will let opportunists rapidly clone successful games and flood storefronts, burying originals under low-effort copies. A discoverability-and-design-economics angle on how fast generative tooling is changing what shipping a game on Steam looks like.
picks.rationale: A macro analyst view on AI-cloning as a discoverability threat — distinct from the specific Meccha clone incident already published — that changes how devs think about differentiation and launch strategy on storefronts.
